title: Explore and use a variety of strategies to learn (revised)

lessons.title: How people learn
lessons.html:
Everyone can learn

Learning does not stop when you leave school. On the farm we learn new things all the time: a new tractor, a new spray, a new way to treat sick animals, a new computer system for records. People who keep learning do their jobs better, stay safe and can get better jobs.

Different ways of learning

People learn in different ways. Most people use more than one.

  • Seeing: watching someone show you, looking at pictures, posters and diagrams.
  • Hearing: listening to explanations, talking about it, asking questions.
  • Doing: trying it yourself with your hands, practising.
  • Reading and writing: reading a manual or label, writing notes.

Think about something you learned well, for example driving or milking a cow. How did you learn it? Most likely someone showed you, explained it and then let you practise. That mix of seeing, hearing and doing works very well.

What helps learning

  • Being rested and not hungry.
  • A quiet place without too much noise.
  • Knowing why you need to learn something.
  • Learning a little at a time, not everything at once.
  • Practising often.
  • Someone to ask when you are stuck.

What gets in the way

  • Being afraid to ask questions or to make mistakes.
  • Worry, stress or tiredness.
  • Not understanding the language that is used. Ask for words to be explained.

Remember: asking a question is not a sign of weakness. It shows that you want to get it right. A good trainer or supervisor is happy when you ask.

lessons.title: Strategies you can use
lessons.html:
Tools for learning

Ask questions

Questions help you understand. Use question words: what, why, how, when, where, who. For example: "Why do we close the dip tank lid?" "How many litres do I put in?"

Take notes

Write down short points, not every word. Use your own words. You can draw a simple picture or arrow. Keep your notes in one small book so you can read them later.

Break it into steps

A big job is easier when you break it into small steps. Learn one step, then the next.

  1. Watch the whole job once.
  2. Do step one with help.
  3. Do step one alone. Then add step two.
  4. Keep going until you can do the whole job.

Memory tricks

  • Repeat things out loud or in your head.
  • Make a short word from the first letters. For example, FIFO means First In, First Out.
  • Link it to something you already know. "The cold room is like a fridge at home, but bigger."
  • Teach someone else. When you explain it to a co-worker, you remember it better.

Use what is around you

  • Labels, posters and safety signs.
  • Manuals and booklets.
  • The LMS lessons on a phone or computer.
  • Experienced workers, your supervisor, the extension officer or the vet.
  • The library or the radio.

Learn from mistakes

Everyone makes mistakes. When something goes wrong, ask: What happened? Why? What will I do differently next time? Then try again. On the farm, report mistakes that affect safety or animals at once, so they can be fixed.

lessons.title: Planning your learning
lessons.html:
Being in charge of your own learning

You learn best when you know what you want to learn and make a plan.

Set a goal

A goal says what you want to be able to do. Make it clear and possible. For example: "In two months I want to be able to read the feed mixing sheet without help." A goal like "I want to know everything" is too big.

Make a simple plan

What I want to learnHow I will learn itWho can helpBy when
Read the feed sheetPractise each morning with the supervisorMr KhumaloEnd of June
Finish two LMS lessonsRead on my phone during lunchTraining officerFriday

Find time

Many workers learn in small pieces of time: during lunch, on the bus, or for 15 minutes after supper. Small, regular learning is better than one long session once a month.

Check your progress

  • Can I do it now without help?
  • What is still difficult?
  • Do I need to try a different way, for example watching instead of reading?

If one way of learning does not work for you, try another. Ask the trainer to show you again, find a picture, or practise more.

Working with others

Study groups help. Two or three co-workers can read a lesson together, ask each other questions and share notes. Help each other, but do your own quiz so you know what you have learned.

Key points

  • People learn by seeing, hearing, doing, and reading and writing – a mix works best.
  • Ask questions; it shows you want to get it right.
  • Break big jobs into small steps and practise often.
  • Use memory tricks like repeating, short words and teaching others.
  • Set a clear goal, make a plan and check your progress.
